primitives.name: Perspective Volume Field
primitives.verbatim_quote: Rise and look from the hill-top at the distant view ; represent to yourself as vividly as possible the distance of the uttermost horizon ; and then with inverted head look at the same.

primitives.breakdown_regime: Inversion of head orientation alters perceived depth extent.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that depth perception is not an isolated sensory modality but part of a triadic structure with breadth and height. This implies that the visual field is inherently a volume, and that changes in one dimension affect the others. The inversion experiment shows that depth sensation is sensitive to head orientation, which suggests that ocular muscle activity contributes to depth perception. The physiological absence of pupil or muscle strain indicates that depth perception is not merely a mechanical reflex but involves higher-order cognitive processing. The functional interdependence of dimensions means that depth is not absolute but relative, and thus subject to perceptual modulation. The failure mode occurs when one dimension is compromised, leading to a cascade of misperception across all dimensions. The mathematical structure is a ternary relational system where D(f(B,H)) and H(f(B,D)) and B(f(H,D)).
